subject.title: fix(session-memory): bound session transcript file read with size cap

question: Should the session-memory hook adopt the existing shared transcript-streaming reader, or is its descriptor-bound fixed 50 MiB tail intentionally the canonical contract for reset-memory extraction?
rationale: Both approaches can bound memory, but choosing a distinct reader and an explicit content-loss boundary is an ownership and long-term behavior decision that source review cannot safely infer from this small PR alone.

options.title: Align with the shared reader
options.body: Refresh against current main and reuse or extend the shared transcript-reading primitive if it can retain the same bounded-memory and descriptor-safety guarantees.

options.title: Keep the dedicated 50 MiB policy
options.body: Accept the local descriptor-bound reader only after confirming that the session-memory hook deliberately needs this separate fixed-window degradation contract.

recommendation.title: Align with the shared reader
recommendation.body: Refresh against current main and reuse or extend the shared transcript-reading primitive if it can retain the same bounded-memory and descriptor-safety guarantees.

likelyOwner.reason: The shared transcript-streaming implementation is the closest existing behavior to evaluate as the canonical path.
